resources.string: Local-only viewer for Bebird Wi-Fi scopes
Switch the scope on. The app listens for it over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi; tap it to join its Wi-Fi and open the picture.
Tap Find nearby to look for a switched-on scope.
No scope found nearby. Make sure it is switched on and close by.
%1$d scope(s) nearby. Tap one to connect.
Could not join %1$s. Make sure the scope is switched on and try again.
Joined %1$s, but no camera answered. Try again, then share the debug log below if it keeps happening.
Choose the scope\'s Wi-Fi in the dialog…
Could not join the scope\'s Wi-Fi. Make sure it is switched on and try again.
Can\'t see it? Pick its Wi-Fi
%1$d remembered scope(s). Tap one to connect, or Find nearby to listen for others.
It will no longer be listed until you join it again. Android may still remember your approval of its Wi-Fi.
Nearby scanning needs the permissions Android just asked for. Location is only so Android will list Wi-Fi networks; the app never reads where you are.

Everything the app does while finding and joining scopes is recorded here. Share it (for example to the Claude app) to get help; it includes nearby network names and addresses. Hide puts this card away until the next shake.
Debug log revealed. Shake again any time.
Debug log copied to the clipboard.
EarDigger only ever sends packets to the camera\'s own address on the local network. Bluetooth and Wi-Fi scanning only listen on this phone. No accounts, no analytics, no update checks, no cloud.
Lost the scope\'s Wi-Fi. Is it still switched on?
